description: Add a receipt to the user's savings record: one row per line (generic item, quantity, unit, paidMinor in cents, optional offerId from search_offers). Each line is stored with its price range around the store that day (cheapest, typical, priciest) and returns savings vs each plus the percentile; negative savings (paid above typical) are kept. Lines on a thin range are shown but not totalled. Each line has `basis` (what it was compared with) or `notCounted` (why not) and a plain `summary`; the receipt has a `summary`, `method` and `methodUrl` (how savings are counted, an estimate compared with typical prices nearby) to pass on to the user. Append-only and idempotent: reuse `operationId` to retry safely; to fix a purchase, record a new one with `supersedesPurchaseId`.

basis.description: receipt: read from a receipt; user_report: the user said so.

item.description: The generic item, as compare_items takes it: "chicken thighs", "large eggs", "bananas". Not a brand or receipt code.

label.description: The receipt's own wording, kept as is.

offerId.description: The flyer offer bought, if known (from search_offers).

paidMinor.description: What the line cost, in cents (after line discounts). null if unknown.

near.description: The store's postal code, or the shopper's; sets which stores the range is drawn from.

operationId.description: A stable id for this write (e.g. a UUID you generate once per receipt). Replaying it returns the same receipt.

storeId.description: The store's id from stores_near, when known.

supersedesPurchaseId.description: A purchase this one corrects; the old one stays stored but leaves the totals.

name: record_purchases
title: Record a purchase in the savings record
